occurrences.checkable_against: The recently published research methodology, interview list, and transcripts
occurrences.quote_span: In recently published research , I interviewed senior policymakers, regulators, and accreditors in England and the United States and asked them what they understood by quality.
occurrences.speaker: Nicola Dandridge
occurrences.subject: higher education quality regulation in England and the United States

occurrences.checkable_against: The reviewed studies of higher education regulatory systems and their stated outcomes
occurrences.quote_span: Several studies of regulatory systems have examined administrative burden from the institutional perspective but not their impact on students’ education.
occurrences.speaker: Nicola Dandridge
occurrences.subject: higher education quality regulation in England and the United States

occurrences.checkable_against: Historical higher education regulatory frameworks, tuition-fee and sector-expansion records, and English framework conditions
occurrences.quote_span: More recently, coinciding with increased tuition fees and an expanded sector, more formal regulatory approaches have been adopted with mandatory “ do no harm ” requirements and the English regulatory framework conditions.
occurrences.speaker: Nicola Dandridge
occurrences.subject: higher education quality regulation in England and the United States

occurrences.checkable_against: Historical higher education quality-assurance and regulatory frameworks in England and the United States
occurrences.quote_span: In both the United States and England, regulation has until recently largely taken the form of peer review or co-regulation, aimed at improvement and enhancement (and indeed the word “regulation” was rarely used in this context).
occurrences.speaker: Nicola Dandridge
occurrences.subject: higher education quality regulation in England and the United States

occurrences.checkable_against: The reviewed evaluations’ stated limitations and methodologies
occurrences.quote_span: Some cited insufficient time to observe effects; others pointed to inadequate data and methodological challenges .
occurrences.speaker: Nicola Dandridge
occurrences.subject: higher education quality regulation in England and the United States

occurrences.checkable_against: Surveys and official submissions documenting university complaints about higher-education regulatory burden and compliance costs
occurrences.quote_span: Complaints about regulatory burden are common , and universities understandably emphasize compliance costs.
occurrences.speaker: Nicola Dandridge
occurrences.subject: higher education quality regulation in England and the United States

occurrences.checkable_against: The corpus of evaluations of quality regulation reviewed in the research
occurrences.quote_span: No evaluations examined institutional autonomy as a factor, despite conventionally held theory that autonomy leads to better outcomes.
occurrences.speaker: Nicola Dandridge
